open_decisions.question: In AUDPROC the audit timestamp is moved into AUD-TIMESTAMP (line 74) and then overwritten by the group move of the 32-byte system information into the 58-byte AUD-HEADER (line 75), so the written audit record carries neither the timestamp nor correctly aligned system/user/program/terminal values. On open failure the program also closes the unopened audit file. Must the forward audit service reproduce the record exactly as written today, or write the timestamp and the system, user, program and terminal identifiers in their own fields?

Copybook AUDITLOG declares audit types ('TRAN','USER','SYST'; BR-143), actions (CREATE, UPDATE, DELETE, INQUIRE, LOGIN, LOGOUT, STARTUP, SHUTDOWN; BR-144) and outcome statuses ('SUCC','FAIL','WARN'; BR-145). Callers assign them and AUDPROC writes them unchecked. Must the forward audit service reject values outside these domains, or record whatever the caller supplies (as implemented)?

DB2ERR (line 75) uses the non-standard 'ACCEPT WS-CURRENT-TIMESTAMP FROM TIME STAMP'; the ERRPROC logic file flags the same construct (line 57) and PORTDEL uses it for the deletion audit timestamp (source line 169). Which compiler extension is in use and what timestamp format do ERRLOG rows, error-log records and deletion audit records actually carry?

Fifteen elementary level-01 items (e.g. HISTLD00 WS-COMMIT-THRESHOLD, the REPORT-RECORD print lines, DB2CONN WS-CONNECTION-STATE/WS-RETRY-COUNT/WS-MAX-RETRIES, DB2CMT WS-SAVEPOINT-ID) are catalogued as record-level items without Field IDs, so no Java type could be assigned. Should the reverse harness register Field IDs for them, or may later stages map them at record level using the catalogued PIC?

AUDPROC appends audit records to a sequential dataset (DD AUDFILE, OPEN EXTEND per call), its group MOVE LS-SYSTEM-INFO TO AUD-HEADER may overwrite the timestamp just set, and it CLOSEs the file after a failed OPEN; RPTAUD00 meanwhile reads an indexed audit file keyed AUD-KEY (DD AUDITLOG) built on the same copybook. Is there one audit trail (and which organisation), and must the timestamp overwrite be reproduced?

ERRPROC's LINKAGE LS-ERROR-REQUEST is 354 bytes, but DB2ERR (line 199) and DB2STAT (line 227) CALL 'ERRPROC' USING ERR-MESSAGE from copybook ERRHAND (about 370 bytes, different field order). Which layout is the contract of the Java error service?

COPY PORTREC (PORTTRAN line 40) is missing from the repository, so FD PORTFOLIO-FILE (record PORTFOLIO-RECORD, RECORD KEY PORT-ID, read and REWRITTEN by PORTTRAN) has no layout. Which copybook or record definition is authoritative for this file?

Ten elementary level-01 FD/WS items have no permanent Field ID (PORTTRAN WS-EOF-FLAG, TSTGEN00 SEED-RECORD, TSTVAL00 EXPECTED-RECORD/ACTUAL-RECORD/REPORT-RECORD, UTLMNT00 ARCHIVE-RECORD/REPORT-RECORD, UTLVAL00 ERROR-RECORD, FILEHNDL INPUT-RECORD/OUTPUT-RECORD). Should the reverse data agent register Field IDs for record-level elementary items so their Java types can be fixed?

Which character encoding do the DISPLAY files of this batch use (assumed EBCDIC code page 037), and must Java preserve EBCDIC collation for indexed keys such as PORT-KEY, VSAM-RECORD-KEY, POS-KEY and TRAN-KEY?

Which character encoding (code page) do the files and areas described by these copybooks use for DISPLAY data on the legacy platform (EBCDIC 037, 1140, another EBCDIC variant, or ASCII)? The zoned-decimal test vectors and String codecs depend on it.

Several data names are declared more than once: CK-FILE-STATUS (CKPRST group line 35 and child line 38); ERR-VALIDATION/ERR-PROCESSING/ERR-SECURITY (RETHND level-88 and STD-ERROR-CODES fields); RC-SUCCESS..RC-CRITICAL, TRN-TYPE-BUY/SELL/FEE, ERROR-CODE and ERROR-ROUTINE across COMMON, RETHND and TRNREC. What Java naming convention should disambiguate them (for example record-qualified class members keyed by Field ID)?

GAP-003 (critical): PORTTRAN copies PORTREC at line 40 under FD PORTFOLIO-FILE, but no PORTREC copybook exists; PORT-ID, PORT-TOTAL-UNITS, PORT-TOTAL-COST, PORTFOLIO-RECORD, PORT-ACCOUNT-NO and PORT-RECORD have no Field IDs. Where is the authoritative PORTREC layout (load library, external PDS, vendor library), or should PORTTRAN's portfolio file be specified with another existing layout such as PORTFLIO?

BR-111 to BR-114 describe confirmed dead code in PORTTRAN: 2200-UPDATE-POSITIONS is never performed, so the routing by type (BU -> 2210-PROCESS-BUY, SL -> 2220-PROCESS-SELL, TR -> 2230-PROCESS-TRANSFER reporting 'Transfer processing not implemented', FE -> 2240-PROCESS-FEE), the sale check 'PORT-TOTAL-UNITS < TRN-QUANTITY' -> 'Insufficient units for sale', the position arithmetic (buy: units += quantity, cost += amount; sell: units -= quantity, cost -= amount; fee: cost -= amount) and the audit mapping (BU -> 'CREATE', SL -> 'DELETE', TR/FE -> 'UPDATE') never execute. Validated transactions are only counted. Should the forward system (a) keep the as-found behaviour (validate and count only), or (b) implement the designed but unreachable position update, short-sale check and audit trail, or are these applied elsewhere?

GAP-076: CALL 'ERRPROC' USING ERR-MESSAGE (line 316) passes the 370-byte ERRHAND record ERR-MESSAGE, while ERRPROC receives the 354-byte LS-ERROR-REQUEST; the layouts are offset by 18 bytes. Which error-record layout is authoritative for errors reported by PORTTRAN, and should the forward error reporting reproduce the shifted fields?
